references.sentence: As shown in Fig. 10.3.1, the MCCOPA consists of an AC-coupled high frequency path (HFP) and a chopped low-frequency path (LFP).
To ensure a wide CMVR, CHin is implemented by capacitively-driven MOSFETs MN1-4 (Fig. 10.3.2) located in a floating N-tub, capable of withstanding 100V [1].
In this design, this chopper ripple is suppressed by a SC RRL (Fig. 10.3.1) [1].
The offset of GmR1 itself is auto-zeroed according to the timing diagram shown in Fig. 10.3.1.
Measurements on 14 samples show that its input offset is less than 3μV (Fig. 10.3.3(a)), while its input offset current is below 95pA and its input bias current is less than 107pA.
The MCCOPA’s DC PSRR is greater than 120dB, while its DC CMRR is greater than 148dB (Fig. 10.3.3(b)).
The input-referred noise density is 55nV/√Hz, which is flat down to ~1Hz (Fig. 10.3.4(a)).
Due to the multipath architecture, the transfer-function notch caused by the RRL is filled, Fig. 10.3.4(b).
Differential step responses at 0V and 20V DC input CM voltages are shown in Fig. 10.3.5(a).
Fig. 10.3.5(b) shows the step response with (above) and without (below) the multi-path architecture, respectively.
The MCCOPA’s CM step response is shown in Fig. 10.3.5(c).
In Fig. 10.3.6 the MCCOPA’s performance is summarized and compared to the state-of-the-art opamps.
